## Data sources

| Source | What it has | Format | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| [PATH Ridership Statistics](https://www.panynj.gov/path/en/about/stats.html), Port Authority of NY & NJ | Monthly reports (2012–present) and hourly reports (2017–present, plus Jul 2014 and Nov 2016 snapshots), **by station** | PDF only: no API, no CSV | **Main source for all charts** |
| [FTA National Transit Database: Complete Monthly Ridership](https://data.transportation.gov/d/8bui-9xvu) (PATH = NTD ID 20098) · [NTD monthly ridership page](https://www.transit.dot.gov/ntd/monthly-ridership) | Monthly system-wide unlinked trips, 2002–present | CSV / API | Cross-check |
| [NY Open Data: PATH Monthly Ridership, Beginning 1996](https://data.ny.gov/d/v5t9-im68) ([data.gov listing](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/port-authority-trans-hudson-path-monthly-ridership-beginning-1996)) | Monthly system total in thousands. **Stopped updating in 2016** | CSV / API | Cross-check |
| [NY Open Data: PATH Average Weekday & Weekend Ridership, Beginning 1996](https://data.ny.gov/d/p7e4-ipty) ([data.gov listing](https://catalog-beta.data.gov/dataset/port-authority-trans-hudson-corporation-path-average-weekday-and-weekend-ridership-be-1996)) | Average weekday and weekend ridership, system total. Stopped in 2016 | CSV / API | Not used (covered by PDFs) |
| [APTA Quarterly Ridership Reports](https://www.apta.com/research-standards/ridership/) ([archive](https://www.apta.com/news-research/public-transit-statistics/ridership-data/archives/)) | Quarterly unlinked trips by agency (listed as "Port Authority of NY & NJ", heavy rail) | PDF | Not used (quarterly, system only) |


**Why PDFs, when there are CSVs?** The two free machine-readable sources don't cover what
this project needs. NY Open Data **stopped in 2016**. The National Transit Database is
current but has **system totals only**, with no stations and no hours. The Port
Authority's PDFs are the only source with station-level and hourly detail up to the
present. So the PDFs are the main source, and the CSV/API sources are used to check them.

The PDFs live at `https://www.panynj.gov/content/dam/path/about/statistics/<file>.pdf`.
File names vary by year (`2012_PATH_Ridership_Report`, `2015-PATH-Ridership-Report`,
`…-hourly-…` vs `…-Hourly-…`), so `scripts/01_download.py` lists each one explicitly.

## Pipeline: step by step

| Step | Script / file | Input → output | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Download | `scripts/01_download.py` | PANYNJ, NY Open Data and NTD URLs → `data/raw/` | Downloads 15 monthly and 12 hourly PDF reports, plus the two CSV/API sources. Checks each PDF is valid and skips files already on disk. |
| 2. Parse monthly | `scripts/02_parse_monthly.py` | `data/raw/pdf/monthly_*.pdf` → `data/processed/path_monthly_by_station.csv`, `path_monthly_system.csv`, `crosscheck_system_totals.csv` | Reads the PDF text layer (`pdfplumber`), finds each month's page, extracts both station tables and the day-count row, standardises station names, validates, and compares with NY Open Data and NTD. |
| 3. Parse hourly | `scripts/03_parse_hourly.py` | `data/raw/pdf/hourly_*.pdf` → `data/processed/path_hourly.csv`, `hourly_parse_issues.csv` | Reads every station page (section label, station, 24 hours × 8 columns) and reshapes it to a long "tidy" table. Any row it can't parse is logged. |
| 4. Charts | `pathviz.py` | processed CSVs → Plotly figures | One module defines every chart, so the dashboard and the presentation always match. |
| 5. Publish | `path/dashboard.qmd`, `path/slides.qmd`, `_quarto.yml` | → website (`_site/`) | Quarto renders the dashboard, slides and this page. GitHub Pages hosts them. |

```bash
python scripts/01_download.py      # step 1
python scripts/02_parse_monthly.py # step 2
python scripts/03_parse_hourly.py  # step 3
quarto render                      # steps 4–5
```

### Problems the parser handles

* **Two tables per page.** Each station appears twice on a monthly page: first as totals
  and averages, then as average-daily and totals by day type. The parser tells them
  apart by order.
* **Renamed stations.** "Pavonia/ Newport" → "Newport", "WTC" → "World Trade Center",
  "Christopher St." → "Christopher Street".
* **Section labels change format** across years ("January 2021", "Jun 2025", "2026-Jan",
  "YTD 2019", "2025 Annual"), and ASCII and Unicode hyphens are mixed.
* **Blank holiday columns** in months with no holiday (e.g. Mar, Apr and Aug 2026) leave
  6 values per row instead of 8.
* **One-off snapshot reports** (July 2014, November 2016) use slightly different headers.
* **macOS file names are case-insensitive**, so `Hourly.pdf` and `hourly.pdf` would
  overwrite each other. Files are saved as `hourly_2025.pdf` etc.

## Validation

All checks run automatically every time the scripts run. A failed check stops the pipeline.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| All 13 stations present every month | 178 of 178 months |
| Station rows add up exactly to the NY subtotal, NJ subtotal and system total printed in each PDF | Passed for every month |
| Weekday + Saturday + Sunday + holiday totals = monthly total (±2 for rounding) | Passed for every station-month |
| vs. NY Open Data (independent, 48 overlapping months) | Median difference 0\.01%, max 0\.33% (NY Open Data is rounded to thousands) |
| vs. National Transit Database (independent, 177 months) | NTD runs 6–11% higher every month, as expected, because NTD counts every boarding (unlinked trips). Month-to-month movements match. |
| Hourly: each page's 24 hour-rows add up to its printed "Total" row | All 1\,820 station-pages pass (±30 for rounding) |
| Hourly vs. monthly report: system weekday entries | Within 1\.8% every year |

## Data definitions

**What is counted.** Every number comes from PATH's **faregates**, the turnstiles and
TAPP gates riders pass through. There are two kinds of count:

| Term | What it means | Which station it describes | Where it's used |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Entry** (also "trip" or "ridership") | A person passing *into* the system through a faregate | The **origin**: the station where the trip **starts** | Monthly data (all charts on the Overview and Monthly pages), and the hourly charts unless marked "exits" |
| **Exit** | A person passing *out* through a faregate | The **destination**: the station where the trip **ends** | Hourly data only, where marked |

*Example:* someone who commutes from Hoboken to 33rd Street and back counts as an
**entry at Hoboken** in the morning and an **entry at 33rd Street** in the evening. That's
two trips. Their morning **exit** is counted at 33rd Street.

**How exits are counted.** PATH riders tap in only. Nobody taps out, so exits **don't
come from fare payments**. The hourly reports are labelled *"Turnstile Count"* (through
2023) and *"Legacy and TAPP Faregates Count"* (from 2024). Exits are the number of people
physically passing **out through the exit turnstiles or faregates**, and the gate counts
each passage without charging. Because entries and exits aren't linked to a card, the data
**can't say where a particular rider went**. There are no origin–destination pairs, only
how many trips started and ended at each station.

**Entries vs. exits don't match system-wide after 2021.** Through 2019, system-wide
weekday exits were within about 1% of entries, as expected. Since 2022 exits have run
**about 9–12% higher** than entries. The reports don't explain this. Possible reasons
include entries that aren't counted (cross-honor, freewheeled, fare evasion) and
differences between the old and new gates. For this reason the dashboard uses **entries**
for all ridership totals, and uses exits only to show *when* trips end.

**Other terms**

* **Average weekday / Saturday / Sunday / holiday.** Total entries on that type of day,
  divided by the number of those days in the month. **Holidays** are days PATH runs a
  holiday schedule, and they're left out of the weekday, Saturday and Sunday averages.
* **Rush hours.** In this project: 7–9 am and 5–7 pm (four one-hour periods).
* **Cross-honor.** Tickets from other operators (e.g. NJ Transit) that PATH accepts during
  service disruptions. These are **not** included in the counts.
* **Freewheeled entries.** Excluded from 2024 on, per the report headers. The reports don't
  define the term. It usually means gates set to free entry, with no fare charged.
* **Legacy + TAPP.** From 2023, counts combine the old turnstiles and PATH's new contactless
  **TAPP** faregates.
* **Linked vs. unlinked trips.** The PATH reports count *linked* trips: one faregate entry
  per journey, even if the rider changes trains. The federal National Transit Database
  counts *unlinked* trips, meaning every boarding, so a transfer counts twice. That's why
  NTD totals run about 6–11% higher than the PATH reports every month.


## Data dictionary

::: {.dict}
**`data/processed/path_monthly_by_station.csv`**: one row per station per month.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | date | First day of the month |
| `year`, `month` | int | Calendar year and month (1–12) |
| `station` | text | Station name (13 stations) |
| `state` | text | `NJ` or `NY` |
| `total` | int | Entries in the month |
| `avg_weekday`, `avg_saturday`, `avg_sunday`, `avg_holiday` | int | Average entries per day of that type |
| `avg_daily` | int | Total ÷ days in the month |
| `weekday_total`, `saturday_total`, `sunday_total`, `holiday_total` | int | Total entries on all days of that type |
| `n_weekdays`, `n_saturdays`, `n_sundays`, `n_holidays` | int | Number of days of each type in the month |

**`data/processed/path_monthly_system.csv`**: same columns, one row per month for the whole
system (no `station` / `state`).

**`data/processed/path_hourly.csv`**: long format, one row per period × station × hour ×
day type × direction.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `year` | int | Report year |
| `period` | text | `month` (one month) or `annual` (whole-year or year-to-date average) |
| `month` | int | 1–12 when `period` is `month`, blank otherwise |
| `station` | text | Station name, or `System-wide` |
| `hour` | int | Hour of day, 0–23 (0 = midnight to 1 am) |
| `day_type` | text | `weekday`, `saturday`, `sunday`, `holiday` |
| `direction` | text | `entry` (trip starts here) or `exit` (trip ends here) |
| `avg_count` | int | Average number of people through the faregates in that hour |

**`data/processed/crosscheck_system_totals.csv`**: monthly PDF totals next to NY Open Data
(`nyod_thousands`) and NTD (`upt`, unlinked passenger trips), with % differences.
:::

## Limitations

* **Faregate entries are not unique people.** A daily commuter makes about 40 trips a
  month. Fare evasion, cross-honored and freewheeled entries are not counted.
* **Closures show up as near-zero values, not as missing data.** Examples: WTC and Exchange
  Place weekends in much of 2014, Hoboken in February 2025 (about 2,700 a weekday and zero on
  weekends), and low WTC weekend values in 2019. They're real counts, but they pull
  averages down.
* **Hourly data starts in 2017**, plus one-month snapshots for July 2014 and November 2016.
  Exits are only available in the hourly data.
* **The current year is partial** (through the latest published month).
* **Fare-system change.** The move from old turnstiles to TAPP faregates (2023–25) changed
  the counting equipment. Small shifts in that period may partly reflect measurement.
* **Rounding.** The PDFs round averages to whole people, so sums of hourly values can be off
  by a few.
